intro.en:
Uncertain times for our fragile, vagabond hero, Rafael Yaluff.

Fear, remorse, suspicion of self and future, loom day after day with more authority.

The windmills vanish, giving way to the bleakness of 9 to 5, along its pixelated sharpness.

In this feature: 3 years of dodged waves in a sea of tar.

I hope you enjoy them like artifacts in an arid game. Useful? Maybe only if they are able to hang on invisible walls.
intro.es:
Tiempos inciertos para nuestro frágil héroe vagabundo, Rafael Yaluff.

Miedo, remordimiento, sospecha exacerbada de sí mismo y del futuro, acaecen día tras día, con mayor autoridad.

Los molinos del viento se desvanecen, dando paso a la ineludible tarea de 9 a 5 y junto a ella la pixelada nitidez.

En esta entrega: 3 años de olas capeadas en un mar de petroleo.

Espero las disfrute como artefactos en un árido juego. ¿Útiles? Tal vez solo sí consiguen colgar de muros invisibles.

intro.en:
I paint plein air in the southern rainforest of Chile, and my work focuses on searching for a language for this experience. The impressionism of Claude Monet and my interest for Husserl’s phenomenology is what I bring with me.

I experiment with different ways of perception related to the constitution of objects, my interest focuses on how they appear to consciousness, from a synthesis that goes from sensitive ingredients, like colors, to something we intuit: an object – a landscape. I try to compose my painting as a system of available elements, by working in a state of objectual privation that pursues to suspend my awareness of the apparent landscape, and thus approach an abstract material level in front of me –a basic and sensitive moment of object-free qualities.

I am not aiming towards a deconstruction of the rendered object or an archaeology of its emergence on the basis of its image, but to work in a state of availability “making oneself available to the thing that is being born and that is still shapeless like molten rock. Undefined. Confuse. Non-delineated” (F. Fellini). Refraining objective rendering, preserving therefore the objective synthesis as unrealized.

The hypothesis is that, when this procedure is achieved successfully, what we experience with the finished painting is a phenomilalisation of the available material: There a metabolic change, and in this sense something immanent appears and becomes the apparent phenomenon. We could say in this specific sense that the painting moves us, because although what we are facing is a mere artifice, incapable of moving on its own, it can summon movement by leading us towards synthesis, and thus taking part in it’s generation. Movement is a quality of life, and in this sense, we can say that the painting gives the feeling of life, because it asks consciosness to unfold itself as it does in the natural-vital visual experience, in which we do not see images, but their possibilities.

As opposed to the static experience of work based on photographic referent, when painting plain air one experiences the strength and ambiguity of the phenomenon itself. And we can delve into its modality, limited only by ourselves. So then, the project is to encapsulate the emergence of a phenomenon into a pictorial device, a painting that preserves the synthesis in potential mode, and once enacted by the gaze of a spectator can generate an emergence.

This is the motivation of a genetic realism. It doesn’t aim to be true to the image of the real, but to the originality of the sensitive ingredients upon we co-give, or represent all that is real. It is an attempt to avoid direct contact with representation.

In this portfolio you will see diverse experiments, some related to natural scale phenomenon - which is the reason for some paintings size. And some related to syhthesis. Neither is totally pure or successful, you will see many methodic application flaws. But overall It’s a summary of what my approach to landscape painting has been.

To change our way of seeing requires time and training, during which the eye of the spirit desires boundaries. Understanding is made of empty lines that become sensitive matter, making it comprehensible. Something that I understood in the south is that one should not fear not seeing the end of a painting, because that is the gist of it all: Not to see things in light of their ends, but their beginnings.
